title: The one line, and why paperwork isn't safety
objectives: Use the one line to answer “more funds is safer” in any conversation.
Explain the real cost of clutter: paperwork, statements, tracking.
body_md:
The one line to remember: diversify by what you own, not by how many funds you own. Many clients believe each extra fund adds safety. Often it only adds paperwork: more statements, more funds to track, more decisions — while the portfolio underneath stays the same handful of top stocks. Fewer funds with distinct jobs are easier to review, easier to rebalance, and easier for the client to understand. That understanding is itself a guardrail: a client who can explain their portfolio in one sentence is less likely to panic-sell it.

> **Investor takeaway:** Diversify by what you own, not by how many funds you own.
example: Client with 14 funds: “Let's look at what they hold” — same top stocks, one portfolio, fourteen statements.
